messages:
maya: Quick heads-up — I ran an offline replay against the continuous-batcher heuristics using last week's traces. Found two surprising things: 1) kernel-selection flip at ~128 token windows caused p95 to step up on A100s, 2) KV-cache churn from small prefix mismatches increased effective token cost. Posting a short repro + profiling snapshot.

liam: nice, can you paste the config you replayed with? was this with token_budget=256 or the new adaptive target?

maya: Replay config snippet: ```
# replay config
policy: trace_replay
queue_policy: fifo_prefill
batching: continuous
token_budget_target: 256
kv_cache: enabled
kernel_hint: auto
```

maya: Profiling gist: CPU host queue wait spikes right before kernel switch, kernel selection log shows fallback from fast-attn kernel -> generic kernel at token lengths ~120-140. KV cache traces show many small invalidations due to whitespace-normalization diffs.

liam: Hmm that kernel flip sounds like our selection logic using sample seq_len histogram. Did you use the same kernel-cost table as prod? If the cost estimate changed, scheduler could prefer a different kernel.

maya: I froze the kernel-cost table to prod snapshot (2026-02-22) to isolate. The decision was driven by predicted batch token distribution after queueing — when a few long requests join the batch, the planner switched to a more conservative kernel to avoid OOMs.

rachel: interesting — how frequent were these long requests? can we change queue_policy to reduce the chance of mid-batch long-request arrivals? maybe prefer size-based batching or reserve a fast-path for short sequences?

liam: we have a gated-size policy in experiments: `fifo_prefill + short-first-bias` that tries to fill short-only batches for up to 5ms before relaxing. could test that in replay.

maya: Ran A/B in replay: baseline (fifo_prefill) vs short-first-bias. Results (3M requests trace): baseline p95 token-latency 142ms, A p95 118ms, but A increased median throughput by 6% and slightly increased tail for long requests. KV-cache cost dropped ~3% because short batches had better cache reuse.

samir: Good numbers. Did you measure cost-per-token / GPU utilization? Also curious whether quantized kernels behave similarly.

maya: GPU utilization up ~2% on A, cost-per-token down ~1.8%. Quantized kernel replay shows same kernel flip but with smaller latency penalty (because the quantized fast kernel scales better for the mixed batch).

ops-bot: [replay-run-1747001110] Completed. metrics: {"baseline_p95_ms": "142", "shortbias_p95_ms": "118", "kv_cost_delta_pct": "-3.0", "gpu_util_delta_pct": "+2.0"} :white_check_mark:

rachel: For KV-cache prefix diffs — can we normalize whitespace / canonicalize prefixes before caching? maybe a small prehash step to reduce churn.

liam: we tried canonicalization in 2025-11; it helped but added CPU overhead. Might be worth re-evaluating now that batching strategy reduces per-token kernel overhead. We can add an adaptive canonicalize flag: only run canonicalization for short-request fast-path where it matters.

samir: For offline tuning, propose a replay matrix: vary token_budget_target {128,256,512}, queue_policy {fifo_prefill, short-first-bias, size-aware}, kernel_cost_table {prod, optimistic, pessimistic}. Run each combination on 3 shard traces and collect p50/p95/p99, cost-per-token, kv-churn-rate. We should also run an A/B in the live canary for the top 2 configs.

maya: Agree. I've started a job to spin the matrix. ETA for full matrix on 7-day traces ~18h. Will post CSV to the perf bucket.

rachel: For the A/B harness, we need stable metrics: token-latency p95, model error rate (if available), and upstream request drop rate. Also tag by model family since kernel behavior varies by arch.

liam: FYI — kernel selection logging will need more granularity: include pre-batch seq_len histogram and selected kernel + score delta so we can replay the decision. Adding that to the runtime now.

maya: Plan then: 1) finish replay matrix, 2) run short-first-bias vs baseline on canary infra with ~1% traffic, 3) collect kernel-selection traces + KV-churn histograms, 4) decide on token_budget_target and canonicalize flag. Volunteers to help review results?

liam: I can take the kernel-selection traces.

samir: I'll own the KV-churn analysis and the cost model delta.

rachel: I'll prepare the canary A/B config and dashboard.

maya: Thanks — will upload initial CSVs to gs://redwood-perf-replays/1747001110 and ping the channel when ready. If we see a regression like the kernel flip causing >10% p95 increase we'll rollback the batcher change.

liam: One more ask — include a small synthetic trace that forces mixed short+long mix (10% long) so we can stress the mid-batch kernel decision deterministically.

maya: added. I'll kick that off now.
